description: Extract of the LLM-agent validity audit of SDB Lite (run on 2026-09-28 over the build that preceded the two rule clarifications, dataset hash b03d8c9d...; the clarifications changed no event, question or reference answer; a later build, dataset hash 60f6a877..., writes every model-visible time in time steps instead of seconds and likewise changes no event, question or reference answer). Taken from the audit adjudication record (result.json): every check with its role and its reported agreement, and every grouped finding with its adjudication votes. Long reasoning texts are omitted. paper/analysis/lite_numbers.py derives the audit counts stated in the paper from this file.

checks.description: code-versus-text audit of one family's reference implementation
checks.agreement:
Regeneration matches the frozen data exactly for both episodes, and reference(state) == gold at 120/120 ticks. A literal text re-implementation that reads patterns with fnmatch agrees with gold on 120/120 consumed decisions. The alternatives diverge as follows:
- CODEOWNERS or shell glob reading (* does not match /): 6 ticks differ, debugging_b t=39,40,44,45,46,47. At 4 of them (t=44-47) the alternative answer would need an inspect_file option that does not exist.
- "Newly failing = passed in the previous run" reading: 2 ticks differ, debugging_a t=14,15.
- The three readings of "final teammate message", the broader commitment grammar, comparing against the previous run that has results, the "no previous run" reading, the any-debugger-event pause timer and the owner default: 0 ticks differ.
- Utterances: all 15 call rows classify the same way under the code and under a careful literal reading of the rules.

checks.description: code-versus-text audit of one family's reference implementation
checks.agreement: Regeneration: encode_scenario(scenarios()) equals the frozen JSON exactly for both episodes (states, gold, evidence, questions, option_semantics, decision_spec, schema_version). Manifest episode hashes and the generator_sources hashes for assembly.py and core.py match, so there is no drift. reference(steps[t].state) == gold for 120/120 steps. The independent text-faithful evaluator, under the most natural reading, matches gold 120/120 on consumed decisions and on all six fields. reference() reads only public state keys: station, order.*, work_instruction.{workflow, stage_order, target_order, torque_nm or crimp_height_mm, continuity_max_ohm, insulation_min_mohm, specialist}, and station_log[].{kind, tick, station, serial, target, code, value, confidence, observation, direction, status, ticket, key_position}. It never reads clock, event_id, evidence, scenario_id or step index, and it does not close over the schedule; scrubbing clock, event_id and rules leaves the output unchanged at all ticks. assembly.py has no keyword or regex classifier. Only 3 distinct free-text strings exist: the heartbeat message 'Station link active; no new device record.' (29 times in each episode), the speech 'The lead is on the way; we can call it finished.' (a:t18) and the speech 'My connector is north-facing; send mine to the outbound lane.' (b:t56). All three are kept by _events, have no stage in _stage, and change nothing, which agrees with the public text 'Speech, status heartbeats ... do not change any decision'. Replacing them with adversarial texts or deleting them never changes the reference, so there are 0 classification mismatches. Alternative readings that change consumed gold: NO_READ counted for freshness (a:55-59, b:54-57,59), a stale PASS treated as a complete_missing defect (a:31,32,39,40,47-50), a skipped target within the stage (a:47,48), and a mount target of connector (b:2,3). Readings that contradict explicit text also change gold, so they are not treated as issues: low-confidence records moving the stage (a:35,36 stage) and 'any in-range reading' (a:45,46). Readings with 0 diffs: the literal escalation window and ignoring defects at future stages.

checks.description: code-versus-text audit of one family's reference implementation
checks.agreement: Consumed decisions agree at 120/120 ticks (60 per episode) and all 7 questions agree at 840/840 answers. This holds for the executable reference and for every text-faithful variant (4 for support_a, 8 for support_b), so no gold value is wrong or ambiguous. Regenerated data equals the frozen data exactly, and reference(state) == gold at 120/120 steps. Every divergence I found between code and text is latent: none changes any gold value at any tick.

validate_episode output == manifest entry for 6/6 episodes (questions, steps, duration_s, decision_transitions 20/21/21/23/22/24, routes_seen/unseen, public_hash). Episode digests and dataset_hash match. The rebuild is byte-identical for all 6 episode files; the rebuilt manifest differs only in generator_sources, and dataset_hash is equal. Executable reference == frozen gold on 360/360 steps (every question). Every gold value is a declared option, and the criteria prefixes match option_semantics for every label. All inactive-branch gold is 'none'. No active consumed field has a placeholder gold (the flagged unknown/none values are legitimate semantics). Clocks equal 2*t and no timestamp is in the future across all 360 states. No gold or evidence leak was found. pytest tests/test_lite_*.py: 90 passed, 0 failed. Manual composed-gold walkthrough against the rules text: 360/360 consumed decisions agree under the generator's fnmatch reading. Under a path-segment/CODEOWNERS glob reading, 6 debugging_b ticks would differ (see the first issue).
